references.text: The same law shall apply to the native and to the foreigner who resides among you. This establishes the principle of one law for Israelites and foreigners.
One and the same rule shall apply to you, both to the foreigner and to the native. Same principle of equal legal practice for all.
The foreigner who resides among you shall keep the Passover to the Lord according to the same statute and law. Confirms that foreigners follow the same laws.
The context of the verse, which describes how foreigners are to offer sacrifices in the same way as Israelites.
One law shall apply to the one who sins unintentionally, both to the Israelite and to the foreigner. Repeats the principle of one law later in the same chapter.
You shall not oppress a foreigner or mistreat him, for you were yourselves foreigners in Egypt. Basis for equal treatment of foreigners.
The foreigner who resides with you shall be as one born among you, and you shall love him as yourself. The command to love foreigners as oneself.
Here there is neither Jew nor Greek, slave nor free, male nor female. For you are all one in Christ Jesus. New Testament fulfillment of the principle of equality before God.
The Gentiles who were once foreigners to the covenants have now been brought near by the blood of Christ. Shows how foreigners are included in God's people.
Here there is neither Greek nor Jew, circumcised nor uncircumcised. Christ is all and in all. Confirms the unity of all nations in Christ.
